cohort: 1516 pregnant women at the University Hospital of Getafe (Madrid, Spain) between January 2012 and January 2013
finding: Deliveries following a successful external cephalic version (ECV) are associated with an increased CS rate compared with deliveries of fetuses with spontaneous cephalic presentations.
mod_finding: Women who underwent a successful external cephalic version had a significantly higher cesarean section rate compared with the women in the control group (spontaneous cephalic presentation).
